proposed_from.topic: Quotient-tangent efficiency for nonunique proximal ATE bridges. Work in the dominated observed-data proximal model for O=(Y,A,Z,W,X) whose only bridge restrictions are existence of square-integrable outcome and treatment bridges; neither bridge is unique. Restrict to locally constant closed-range/rank strata and require pathwise differentiability, but do not add bijectivity, surjectivity, or a preferred minimum-norm bridge as a model assumption. Characterize the tangent space and prove an iff criterion for ATE pathwise differentiability. Define the proximal bridge-quotient canonical gradient as the minimum-norm element of the closed affine hull of all valid bridge doubly-robust scores, enlarged if tangent completeness requires it. Prove its efficiency bound and construct a cross-fitted penalized-minimax/Galerkin affine-ensemble one-step estimator with asymptotic linearity, ratio-consistent variance estimation, and Wald coverage under explicit approximation and product-remainder conditions. The hard kernel is the general score-lifting/tangent-normal completeness theorem; a finite constrained-GMM calculation is only a witness. Anchor at Bennett et al. 2023/JRSS-B 2026 Theorems 3 and 6 plus their efficiency boundary, Zhang et al. 2023 Theorem 2.5, Imbens et al. 2025 Theorem 7, and Ai–Shan 2025; distinguish all uniqueness-restricted efficiency results. Cui et al.'s SUPPORT right-heart-catheterization analysis is the consumer: the theorem determines whether bridge-dependent standard errors are globally efficient under redundant proxies and supplies the variance-minimizing replacement. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derived outcome-solvability, treatment-solvability, and null-space-interaction normal generators and showed their closed span equals differences of bridge DR scores. An exact positive 36-cell example with both bridges nonunique has canonical variance 773723312/334026875, and an exact coefficient obstruction shows no single bridge pair attains it. A singular 3-by-3 branch example and four-corner affine-score identities were also checked. Destructive checks covered rank-changing neighborhoods, compact-operator closed-range collapse, Galerkin overclaims, product integrability, and current proximal-efficiency papers; no exact collision was found, but Bennett's final publisher text remains to be checked. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove that scores of actual dominated paths span exactly the annihilator of the three normal classes across the accepted closed-range model, including moving kernels and the arms' shared marginal. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce both finite witnesses, then compare actual tangent-score spans with the proposed normal annihilator in positive 4-by-4 rank-two models with different arm row spaces; an extra unresolved normal direction requires revision. proposed_from.novelty_justification: No novelty is claimed for proximal identification, bridge nonuniqueness, root-\(n\) regular estimation, local efficiency under Zhang et al.'s additional regularity, pair-specific doubly robust inference, Hilbert projection, generalized inverses, operator subspace perturbation, or ordinary cross-fitting. The theorem-level delta is the complete tangent and normal geometry of the bounded likelihood-ratio observed-law intersection with simultaneous nonunique outcome- and treatment-bridge existence, conditional on the explicit score-lifting obligation for its actual path class, and the resulting global affine-hull canonical gradient across bridge pairs. The positive \(36\)-cell chart proves local tangent equality without that general obligation, gives the selected-pair gap \(9496288/200416125\), and gives the nested Chen--Xie outcome-only gap \(1303968/66805375\). The feasible contribution derives efficient-signal convergence from an explicit fold-specific ridge coefficient and deterministic four-corner weight map together with population approximation, foldwise bridge and residual rates, learned-dictionary error, Gram perturbations, ridge bias, exact affine constraints, coefficient envelopes, and a primitive mixed-bias product.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The public arXiv version's Introduction, Theorem 3 and its proof construction, Theorems 6--7, and Conclusion were opened. Theorem 3 validates every primal-dual score pair; Theorems 6--7 fix penalization-selected limits and give normal inference; the paper does not calculate the tangent space or global efficiency bound when both solution sets are non-singleton. The 2026 publisher page returned HTTP 403, so the final text boundary is disclosed.
seed_details.question: Is the tangent closure of the joint two-bridge existence model exactly the annihilator of the outcome-solvability, treatment-solvability, and null-space-interaction normal classes, and is ATE pathwise differentiability equivalent to existence of a square-integrable bridge score?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Bennett et al.'s fixed-solution mixed-bias expansion by a score-lifting theorem for the derivative of the coupled observable restriction map, allowing both kernels to move and both arms to share the \((W,X)\) marginal.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for nonunique proximal bridge tangent spaces, joint bridge existence efficiency, and affine bridge scores found Chen and Xie's one-outcome-bridge generalized-inverse result but no coupled two-bridge tangent-completeness theorem.
seed_details.ambition_reason: The iff regularity frontier and tangent-completeness proof are new model geometry; the scope is important but narrower than a flagship theory of arbitrary ill-posed inverse problems.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Immediate from Chen and Xie because their generalized-inverse tangent calculation already removes bridge uniqueness.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their observable model is generated by the outcome-bridge restriction alone; the joint model adds treatment-solvability and rank-interaction normals through a shared marginal, so its tangent space is strictly smaller in the finite witnesses.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Theorem 3, Lemma 3, the minimum-norm debiasing discussion, and the inference sections were opened. The published construction selects one nuisance limit, whereas score differences over all valid pairs generate a larger affine object.
seed_details.question: Is the canonical gradient the minimum-norm element of the closed affine hull of every valid bridge doubly robust score, and when can one bridge pair attain it?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Project a reference score on the closed span of all pure and four-corner bridge-score differences instead of choosing a minimum-norm bridge function.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for affine-hull influence functions and nonunique proximal efficiency found Severini and Tripathi's one-inverse-problem quotient and Chen and Xie's one-bridge projection, but no two-fiber affine-score characterization or single-pair factorization criterion.
seed_details.ambition_reason: The exact positive nonattainment region turns the projection into a substantive efficiency result rather than a relabeling of a selected bridge score.
seed_details.cynical_objection: A Hilbert-space minimum-norm projection is standard and therefore not publishable.
seed_details.rebuttal: Projection is not claimed as novel; the new content is proving that the actual joint-model gradient affine space equals this hull and that no single bridge pair represents its minimizer on a positive regular chart.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, increasing-moment spectral filtering construction, Theorem 1, efficiency discussion, regularity appendix, and SUPPORT application were opened. Their GMM exploits covariance across moments but assumes a unique finite-dimensional bridge index.
seed_details.question: Can a cross-fitted penalized-minimax or Galerkin ensemble learn the quotient projection and attain its variance under explicit normal-space approximation, Gram stability, and bridge product-remainder conditions?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the unique bridge Jacobian in increasing-moment GMM by an estimated dictionary of pure and four-corner score contrasts, then regularize its empirical Gram operator before cross-fitted evaluation.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for Galerkin affine proximal scores and efficient nonunique bridge ensembles found fixed-representative penalized minimax inference and unique-index joint GMM, but no estimator of the score-affine projection.
seed_details.ambition_reason: The limit law is attached to estimation of a random affine score subspace in two inverse problems and is the feasible attainment half of the efficiency result.
seed_details.cynical_objection: The central limit theorem follows routinely from cross-fitting once an efficient score is known.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nontrivial step is learning the normal subspace and projection weights while retaining affine centering and controlling inverse-problem product error; ordinary one-score cross-fitting does not supply this.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, Propositions 2.3 and 2.5, Lemmas 2.4 and 2.6, the representative-selection construction, and the debiasing section were opened. The results are pointwise in fixed operator ranges and do not analyze local rank changes.
seed_details.question: What is the matched minimax rate and honest confidence frontier as the smallest nonzero bridge-operator singular value approaches zero and a null direction appears?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed adjoint-range criterion by a triangular sequence of singular systems and couple a regularized upper bound to a Le Cam lower bound across adjacent ranks.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for proximal local-to-rank-change inference found a 2026 counterfactual-quantile phase-transition preprint and general source-condition inference, but no ATE theorem for the joint two-bridge rank boundary; the collision makes this a separate, broader project.
seed_details.ambition_reason: A matched local asymptotic frontier is deep, but it changes the fixed-stratum scope and would delay the verified tangent kernel.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Standard weak-instrument or inverse-problem singular-value theory gives the phase transition immediately.
seed_details.rebuttal: The coupled bridge equations can lose different null directions while sharing a marginal, but a full lower-bound construction is not yet available; the seed is deferred rather than padded into the selected core.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, Theorem 3.1, the SUPPORT data-analysis section, and Discussion were opened. The theorem calls the familiar score efficient only at the unique-bridge and surjective-operator submodel, while the application reports bridge-based inference.
seed_details.question: Can the squared projection residual of a fitted bridge score consistently estimate its global efficiency gap and support a local-power test of single-pair attainment?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the uniqueness-based efficiency declaration by a cross-fitted residual regression on estimated pure and four-corner null-score directions.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found Chen and Santos's general Hausman logic and Chen and Xie's one-bridge overidentification diagnostics, but no joint proximal single-pair attainment test.
seed_details.ambition_reason: The diagnostic is concrete and application-facing but depends on the selected tangent theorem and does not carry the proposal alone.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This is an ordinary overidentification test after stacking bridge moments.
seed_details.rebuttal: The null concerns nonlinear single-pair factorization inside an estimated affine score space, not merely whether additional moments vanish.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The nuisance-rate theorems, Theorem 6, and Conclusion were opened together with the abstract and iterated-Tikhonov construction of BennettEtAl2023SourceConditionDR. Those papers adapt across which one of a primal or dual inverse problem is better posed, not across projection dictionaries for two bridge fibers.
seed_details.question: Can affine-ensemble inference adapt to the better of outcome-bridge, treatment-bridge, and normal-projection source conditions while retaining the same Gaussian limit?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Insert iterated Tikhonov estimates for each bridge and the normal regression, then bound the ensemble remainder by the best admissible source-condition product.
seed_details.destination_search: The target-method search found source-condition double robustness for one primal-dual inverse pair but not three-way adaptation including an estimated quotient projection.
seed_details.ambition_reason: The limit law could broaden feasibility, but the projection tangent theorem should be settled before adding source-adaptive tuning.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Bennett et al.'s source-condition double robustness applies componentwise without change.
seed_details.rebuttal: Projection-space estimation creates a third inverse problem and data-dependent affine coefficients; componentwise reuse does not control their joint instability.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The identification and representative-selection sections were opened. Their target is a fixed counterfactual mean, so changing to treatment choice first changes the derivative from one linear mean to a policy-indexed welfare process.
seed_details.question: Can a quotient-invariant proximal policy score deliver regret bounds without selecting unique bridge representatives?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Lift kernel orthogonality from one mean functional to the supremum over a policy class and derive a bridge-invariant stochastic equicontinuity bound for policy differences.
seed_details.destination_search: A direct search found a 2026 public manuscript on decision-aware proximal bridge learning and existing proximal policy-value identification, so a generic policy-regret claim is occupied or too close without a sharper decision boundary.
seed_details.ambition_reason: Policy regret would have high consumer value, but the exact nonunique quotient delta is not yet isolated from recent decision-aware work.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Recent decision-aware proximal bridge learning already controls treatment-selection regret.
seed_details.rebuttal: A quotient-efficient regret frontier may still differ, but the current search cannot defend a clean unoccupied theorem, so the seed is dropped.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The SUPPORT construction and bridge-score inference sections were opened. The data are i.i.d. observational records with no sharp randomization null or time-permutation symmetry.
seed_details.question: Can bridge-representative invariance induce a valid finite-sample permutation or conformal orbit for the proximal ATE?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Construct a group action preserving the joint observed law and the bridge restrictions under a sharp null before inverting a bridge-residual conformity score.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found conformal proximal synthetic-control inference under time symmetry, but no exchangeability group for the cross-sectional observational ATE model; bridge nonuniqueness itself does not create randomization symmetry.
seed_details.ambition_reason: Exact coverage would be attractive, but the maintained experiment does not supply the necessary symmetry.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Permuting treatment is invalid under observational confounding, and permuting bridge representatives is not a sampling symmetry.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds, so the seed is dropped rather than repaired by adding a new experimental or time-series design.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Theorem 1, Remark 3 on covariance-aware GMM, the semiparametric comparison, and SUPPORT application were opened. Their unique finite-dimensional bridge makes the single-pair and affine-ensemble objects coincide by construction.
seed_details.question: Can one derive an observable frontier on which a regularization-selected single bridge pair and the affine ensemble are first-order equivalent, with strict divergence on the other side?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Express the variance gap as the squared distance from the quotient projection to the nonlinear single-pair coefficient variety and characterize its zero set.
seed_details.destination_search: No exact proximal frontier was found; the finite witness shows strict divergence, but a tractable observed-primitive global zero-set formula is not yet available beyond the factorization criterion.
seed_details.ambition_reason: An explicit frontier would strengthen the diagnostic, but the current kernel supports an iff factorization equation rather than a closed-form primitive threshold.
seed_details.cynical_objection: The frontier is merely the tautology that the efficient score belongs to the single-pair family.
seed_details.rebuttal: The four-corner factorization equations give nontrivial observable restrictions, but without a global closed-form threshold the seed is merged only as the attainment theorem.

proposed_from.literature_map: Bennett et al. (2026, public arXiv version Sections 4--6, Theorems 3, 6, and 7) permit nonunique inverse-problem solutions, show that every primal-dual pair yields the mixed-bias score, and obtain cross-fitted inference for fixed penalization-selected limits; they do not assign a global efficiency meaning to pair-dependent variances. Zhang et al. (2023, Propositions 2.3 and 2.5, Lemmas 2.4 and 2.6, and Section 3) characterize identified linear functionals through kernel orthogonality and select a stable representative for debiasing, but do not compute the joint existence-model tangent space. Cui et al. (2024, Theorem 3.1 and Section 6) establish the familiar score as efficient at unique bridges with surjective operators and provide the SUPPORT consumer. Chen and Xie (2026, Lemma 1 and Theorems 2--3) derive a generalized-inverse efficient score after reducing their negative-control model to one outcome-bridge moment; the second bridge existence restriction is absent. Severini and Tripathi (2012, Theorems 2.1--2.4) already establish quotient-style efficiency for nonidentified NPIV functions, so generic projection is not novel. Chen and Santos (2018) provide the tangent-range and overidentification machinery adapted by the score-lifting handle. Ai and Chen (2012) provide orthogonalized sequential-moment information minimization and attaining sieve estimation. Ai and Shan (2025, Theorem 1, Remark 3, and Section 6.2) provide increasing-moment joint GMM and revisit SUPPORT under a uniquely indexed bridge. Imbens et al. (2025, Theorem 7 and Remark 5) keep unique bridges for their efficiency conclusion and identify redundant proxy categories as a source of nonuniqueness. Bennett et al. (2023) provide source-condition and iterated-Tikhonov rate tools. The unoccupied kernel is the complete tangent geometry, quotient canonical gradient, and attaining affine ensemble for the intersection of two existential nonunique proximal bridge restrictions.
